article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Morning Brief
article.dek: McCarthy confirmed he will start Thursday, the rain forecast at MetLife firmed up, and the app board is still nine days old — here is what changed overnight and how to use it.

items.headline: Lead: McCarthy confirmed for Thursday — and the rain forecast firmed up
paragraphs: The one name hanging over Thursday night is settled, and this time it is settled by the player himself. J.J. McCarthy told reporters Wednesday morning he will start against Washington on Thursday night, his first home start as the Giants' starting quarterback, and that he feels fully recovered from the hip injury he picked up Sunday in Philadelphia. He practiced in full on Tuesday, and Cam Skattebo was a full participant too. The Giants are as healthy as they are going to get on a short week.

The other Thursday fact is the sky, and it firmed up overnight. The National Weather Service now calls for rain and possibly a thunderstorm Thursday between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., then rain after 4 p.m., with a 100% chance of precipitation during the day. Thursday night brings more rain, a low around 43, and wind gusting to 22 mph. Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife, outdoors — so expect rain through kickoff, with temperatures falling toward the low 40s.
There is no game today. Week 10 opens Thursday night, and the numbers that matter now are Thursday's: the Giants are -2.5 at DraftKings, with the total at 41.5. Both held steady overnight.
items.takeaway: McCarthy confirmed he will start Thursday, Skattebo is back, and rain is now a near-certainty at MetLife — Thursday's two big questions have answers, a day early.

items.headline: Injuries: Carter and Hood limited, Burks limited, Patrick still in protocol
paragraphs: Beyond McCarthy and Skattebo, Tuesday's practice report had four names to watch. Giants linebacker Abdul Carter (knee/back) was limited, and rookie cornerback Colton Hood (finger) was limited too — Hood is new to the report after leaving practice with a trainer. On Washington's side, receiver Treylon Burks (foot) was limited, and guard Lucas Patrick (concussion) did not practice and must clear protocol before Thursday.

The Giants hold a walkthrough today, and final designations come with the inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff on Thursday. That is the last word if your bet needs a specific name in the lineup. The other Week 10 quarterback spots are as the evening brief left them: Murray likely out 3-4 weeks, Watson set to start Sunday, Lock says he will play, and Beck starts for Arizona.
items.takeaway: Carter and Hood were limited for the Giants, Burks limited and Patrick out for Washington — the inactives about 90 minutes before Thursday's kickoff are the last word on all four.

items.headline: Weather: rain at MetLife on Thursday, and the forecast is now firm enough to plan around
paragraphs: Thursday night at MetLife Stadium is going to be wet, and the forecast is firmer than it was last night. The National Weather Service now puts the chance of rain at 100% during the day Thursday, with a half to three-quarters of an inch possible, and 80% through the night. The kickoff window sits in the Thursday-night period: rain, temperatures falling toward the low 40s, north wind 8 to 11 mph with gusts as high as 22 mph.

This is a forecast fact, not a betting edge. Rain does not pick a side or a total on its own. It is worth knowing because Thursday is outdoors, and because the forecast has firmed up since the evening brief — it was an 80% chance then, and it is a near-certainty now. The final check comes Thursday.
items.takeaway: Rain is forecast at MetLife on Thursday night — 100% chance during the day, 80% at night, wind gusting to 22 mph, temperatures falling toward the low 40s. A forecast fact, not a totals edge.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board is nine days old now — Thursday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the board this morning. It is the same board as last night, byte for byte — generated November 2, still showing Week 8. The app's own freshness field says FRESH, but the timestamp says November 2. The headline cards are from the Bears-Seahawks game: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. The Seahawks moneyline is the example: the app gave Seattle a 60.0% chance to win, while the -175 price needs 63.6% to break even, so the expected value is negative. That is the point — Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the app's plus-EV play — the Bears +3, with the app at 52.4% against a market that priced Chicago at 50.5%, for a small positive edge.

The board has not picked up this week's news either. It still lists Kyler Murray as Minnesota's expected starter — he is now likely out 3-4 weeks with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and Carson Wentz started Monday night. It still lists Sam Darnold as Seattle's starter, though Darnold is ruled out and Drew Lock starts Sunday. Until the board flips to Week 10, there is no card to read for Thursday, so use Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price for Commanders-Giants — the Giants are -2.5 and the total is 41.5 at DraftKings right now — and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override. Thursday game? Thursday check.
items.takeaway: The board is nine days old and still shows last week's Week 8 cards — it still lists Murray and Darnold as starters and knows nothing about McCarthy — so Thursday's Commanders-Giants price goes through Check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value — the price you got matters as much as the pick
paragraphs: Closing line value is a simple idea: did you get a better price than the one the market settled on? If you bet a team at -1.5 and the line closes at -2.5, you beat the closing line by a point. Your bet is the same, but your price was better than the price everyone ended up paying.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you take a favorite at -1.5 on Monday, and by Thursday the same favorite is -2.5 everywhere. You did not win anything yet — the game still has to be played. But you got in a point cheaper than the closing price, and over a season of bets, consistently beating the close is a sign your prices are good. The reverse is true too: if you take -2.5 when -1.5 was sitting there earlier in the week, you gave a point away before kickoff.

That is why the timing of a bet matters, not just the pick. A good price today can be a bad price tomorrow, and a line that moves against you is the market telling you the early price was the better one. Getting the best of the number is a skill of its own — separate from picking winners.
items.takeaway: Closing line value means beating the price the market settles on — take -1.5 when it closes -2.5 and you bought a point cheaper; take -2.5 when -1.5 was there and you gave one away.

items.headline: Thursday's numbers held steady overnight — Giants -2.5, total 41.5
paragraphs: Nothing moved overnight. The Giants are still -2.5 at DraftKings, the total is still 41.5, and the moneyline is still about -135. That is the same board as Tuesday evening — checked this morning against the evening brief, no change on any of the three numbers.

The move already happened, and it happened on the news. The Giants opened as 1.5-point home favorites and are now -2.5. The total opened at 44.5 and is now 41.5 — down three points. The spread moved a point late Monday, once the McCarthy news firmed up. The money is with the move, not against it: reported DraftKings splits from Monday evening had 71% of spread tickets and 89% of the money on the Giants. Tickets and handle agree on New York, so this is not a public-vs-money split — it is a popular side that the money likes too. That is why there is no Fade this morning: a Fade needs the two numbers to disagree, and here they do not.

The app board has caught none of this. It still shows Week 8 prices from November 2 — I checked this morning and it is byte-identical to last night's board — and there is no Commanders-Giants game on it at all. If your book's Thursday number looks different from -2.5 or 41.5, run it through Check and let the app judge your price, not last week's.
items.takeaway: Giants -2.5 and total 41.5 held steady overnight after moving a point and three points respectively since opening — the money agrees with the tickets on New York, so there is no Fade, just a line that has already moved.

items.headline: Thursday is tomorrow — run Check tonight, while your number is still there
paragraphs: The one thing that would have been worth waiting for — McCarthy's status — is answered, by McCarthy himself. The only thing left to wait for is the inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff on Thursday, and that only matters if your bet needs a specific name in the lineup. If it does not, there is nothing left to wait for.

So run Check tonight. Thursday is a short week and the line has already moved once — the Giants went from -1.5 to -2.5 while people waited. If your book has a Thursday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number tomorrow, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
One more thing, while the tracker is open: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too — a record that only keeps the wins is not a record.
items.takeaway: McCarthy is confirmed, so the only wait left is the inactives about 90 minutes before Thursday's kickoff — if Check says bet on your Thursday number, bet it now, and log the losers too.

evidence.fact: VSiN free betting-splits page (data.vsin.com/betting-splits) checked Wednesday Nov 11, about 6:15 a.m. Denver time: the free text view showed only a college basketball game (Florida vs Florida State) with DraftKings splits — spread -8.5, 70% of handle and 72% of bets on Florida; total 164.5, 79% of handle and 62% of bets on the over. No NFL featured row and no DraftKings spread splits for any NFL game were visible in the free tier. Separately, reported DraftKings splits for Commanders-Giants (Covers, Monday evening) show 71% of tickets and 89% of the money on the Giants — tickets and handle agreeing on the same side, which is not a public-vs-sharper disagreement, and DraftKings-only splits alone are insufficient for a Fade.
evidence.interpretation: No qualifying Fade split was available this morning, so the fade slot uses the learning substitute.
evidence.app_guidance: No Fade signal this morning; the learning item teaches closing line value instead.
